physicalNotes: Radius 0.66375348 Jupiter radii from Reller et al. 2026 (2026A&A...712A.142R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...712A.142R/abstract): 47,453.1 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.047 Jupiter masses (Reller et al. 2026, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2026A&A...712A.142R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...712A.142R/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Reller et al. 2026 (2026A&A...712A.142R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname RELLER_ET_AL_2026): P 92.491789 d
sources.shape: Reller et al. 2026 (2026A&A...712A.142R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname RELLER_ET_AL_2026): a/R* 113; Reller et al. 2026 (2026A&A...712A.142R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname RELLER_ET_AL_2026): inclination 90 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Reller et al. 2026 (2026A&A...712A.142R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname RELLER_ET_AL_2026): transit mid-time 2459446.31536 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 3 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
